solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Reading material from singer-songwriter releasing second book as month turned

indicators.note: releasing means letting go, and second says it is the later of the two such letters in the name that goes

parts.note: Bob Dylan is the American singer-songwriter

indicators.note: turned means the two words before it, as and month, are read backwards together

parts.note: as in the sense of for example, abbreviated e.g.
Aug is the short form of August

explanation.surface: Something to read taken from a famous songwriter's catalogue, issued as the month changed.
explanation.walkthrough: BODYLAN is the name less its second B; 'turned' reverses EGAUG to give GUAGE. 'Reading material' is the playful definition: posture and gesture are things people read.
explanation.definitionFit: Gestures and posture are signals people interpret, so non-verbal communication is literally material for reading.

clue.text: Gentry maybe swapping tips on Imperial Ball

indicators.note: the tips of the word Imperial are its first and last letters, so the first of these is exchanged for the last

parts.note: Bobbie Gentry, the American singer of Ode to Billie Joe, is an example of someone surnamed Gentry

explanation.surface: Members of the gentry exchanging gratuities at a grand imperial ball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gentry' looks like the landed classes but is the singer Bobbie Gentry. The tips of 'Imperial' are I and L: the I in her first name becomes L.
explanation.definitionFit: A bobble is a small woolly ball, as on top of a knitted hat.

clue.text: Resource tapped by author and composer (nothing to stop major poet also)

parts.note: Antonín Dvořák was the Czech composer
a major is a musical key, as in C major

indicators.note: to stop means to plug a gap, so the zero letter fills a space inside the poet

parts.note: a bard is a poet
O looks like zero, meaning nothing

explanation.surface: A writer drawing on a composer's music, with a parenthetical aside about a great poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'major poet' reads as a great poet but splits in two. 'Tapped' is the pun: a writer taps away on this layout of typing keys.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dvorak layout is an alternative typing arrangement whose keys a writer strikes when composing text.

clue.text: Intro departs from 70's style rock beat

indicators.note: the intro of a word is its opening letter, which leaves the word for the rock style

parts.note: glam rock was the glittery 1970s style of David Bowie and T. Rex

explanation.surface: A song's intro abandons the beat of seventies-style rock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beat' looks like part of 'rock beat' but is the definition, a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To lam someone is an informal verb for hitting them hard, a thrashing.

clue.text: Childminder involved in murder, say

indicators.note: involved means tangled or intricate, so the letters of in murder say are twisted together

explanation.surface: A childminder caught up in a murder case, supposedly.
explanation.definitionFit: A nursemaid of a nursery looks after young children, which is what a childminder does.

clue.text: Gripped by traumatic uprising, as Egypt was once

indicators.note: uprising means going upwards, which in a down clue reads the letters backwards
gripped by means held inside the word traumatic, so the letters sit within it

explanation.surface: A country caught up in a traumatic revolt, as Egypt has been.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uprising' is topical for Egypt but here turns the letters RAU, held in 'traumatic', upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Egypt and Syria formed the United Arab Republic from 1958, and Egypt kept the title until 1971.

clue.text: Au pairs seen regularly during evening out with a large score to settle

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold

indicators.note: split the phrase into pairs of letters and take every other pair from within it

parts.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Au pairs on an evening out with a big score to settle.
explanation.walkthrough: Split 'evening out' into EV EN IN GO UT and take the second and fourth pairs, EN and GO.
explanation.definitionFit: In football, a sudden-death extra-time goal once ended a drawn match at once, so it was the score that settled things.

clue.text: This requiring change from telephonist (inserting notes unknown)?

definitions.text: This requiring change from telephonist (inserting notes unknown)?

indicators.note: inserting means the following pieces are put inside the rearranged word
change from means the letters of telephonist are altered into a new order

parts.note: nn is the standard abbreviation for notes, plural of n
Y is a mathematical unknown, like x

explanation.surface: A coin-operated phone needed coins from the operator, putting in unknown notes.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: an old coin-operated payphone needed change, unlike the operator's own line.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a machine works when a coin is dropped into it, so it needs small change.

clue.text: Party pop sounds that one can't name

indicators.note: sounds says the two words before it are spoken, and the spoken result is what is entered

parts.note: a do is a party; pop is a word for father, as is da

explanation.surface: Party poppers make noises nobody can put a name to.
explanation.definitionFit: A doodah is an informal word for a thingummy, any object whose proper term escapes you.

clue.text: Large slip or short knickers

indicators.note: short means cut off at the end, so the final letter of the garment word goes

parts.note: bloomers are long loose knickers

explanation.surface: Big slips or shortened knickers: a lingerie drawer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slip' and 'knickers' both look like underwear; slip here means a mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloomer is a British informal word for a big blunder, so a large slip-up.

clue.text: Outstanding work of vicar, not one penning fiction

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, as in a pen, so the falsehood goes inside

parts.note: Rev, short for reverend, is the title of a vicar
a lie is a fiction
O as zero means none, not one

explanation.surface: A clergyman's admirable work, not one given to inventing stories.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outstanding' means projecting, not excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: Relievo is relief sculpture, in which the carving projects, literally stands out, from its background.

clue.text: Thumb's something for grazing on top of flint

parts.note: a lea is a meadow, land where animals graze

indicators.note: top of means the opening letter of the word flint

explanation.surface: A thumb is a handy tool for grazing the top of a flint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thumb' is a verb: to thumb through a book.
explanation.definitionFit: To thumb a book and to leaf through it both mean turning its pages quickly.

clue.text: Balls appearing on Scottish peak keeping small stones hidden no longer

indicators.note: appearing on puts the politician after the rest, tacked on at the end
keeping means holding, so the peak contains the stones

parts.note: Ben is the Scottish word for a mountain, as in Ben Nevis
scree is a mass of small loose stones on a slope
Ed Balls was a prominent Labour politician

explanation.surface: Balls rolling onto a Scottish mountain hide in its small stones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no longer' marks an archaic word. Ed Balls was a senior British Labour politician.
explanation.definitionFit: To bescreen is an archaic verb for to conceal or shelter behind a screen, so the past participle meant covered from view.

clue.text: Fliers kid steals when penniless

parts.note: to kid is to tease, which is to chaff

indicators.note: penniless means without a penny, whose abbreviation P comes out of the word for steals

parts.note: pinches means steals

explanation.surface: A youngster steals when he has no money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kid' looks like a child but is a verb, to tease.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaffinches are common European songbirds, and birds are fliers.

clue.text: Are they invested in for a rainy day? I put on brown coat in case of this

definitions.text: Are they invested in for a rainy day?

indicators.note: put on, in a down clue, places the first piece on top of what follows

parts.note: I as a Roman numeral is one, a single unit

indicators.note: in means the coat goes inside the case of the next word
the case of a word is its outside letters, here those of this

parts.note: rust is a brown coating that forms on iron

explanation.surface: Someone saving for a rainy day dons a brown coat, just in case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brown coat' is not clothing but the coating of oxide on iron.
explanation.definitionFit: These are pooled investment funds bought into as savings, money set aside against hard times.

clue.text: Coach Lendl shaking Murray, at last renewed

indicators.note: renewed means made over again, so the letters are formed afresh into a new order
at last means the final letter of the word Murray

explanation.surface: Tennis coach Ivan Lendl shakes up Andy Murray's game, renewed at last.
explanation.walkthrough: Lendl did coach Murray, so 'Coach' seems tennis; it is a football manager.
explanation.definitionFit: Kenny Dalglish managed Liverpool, Blackburn and Celtic, and a football manager is a coach.

clue.text: Mark one's passing on as standard

definitions.text: Mark one's passing on as standard

parts.words: Mark one's passing on as standard
parts.note: a standard is a flag, which is lowered partway down its pole to mark a death

explanation.surface: Commemorate someone's death in the customary way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standard' looks like 'as usual' but is a flag, and 'passing on' is dying.
explanation.definitionFit: Flags lowered partway are a customary mark of mourning when someone important dies.

clue.text: Pawns crocodile bags in part for wind instrument

indicators.note: bags means grabs and holds, so the line encloses the pawns

parts.note: a crocodile is a line of people walking in pairs, a file
P is the chess abbreviation for pawn, so two pawns are PP

explanation.surface: Someone pawns crocodile-skin bags to pay for part of a musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crocodile' is the British term for a line of schoolchildren walking two by two.
explanation.definitionFit: A fipple is the plug in the mouthpiece of a recorder or whistle that directs the breath.

clue.text: Frank and John cooked

parts.note: john and can are both slang for a toilet
to do food is to cook it, so did means cooked

explanation.surface: Two men, Frank and John, made dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: Both 'Frank' and 'John' look like names; Frank is the definition, an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Candid and frank are synonyms describing someone open and honest in speech.

clue.text: Goofy's dog put in empty reservoir, tragically

indicators.note: tragically means in a disastrous way, so the letters are wrecked into a new order
empty means the word reservoir is emptied of its insides, leaving its outer letters

explanation.surface: Goofy's dog has been dropped in a drained reservoir, with tragic results.
explanation.walkthrough: Goofy is the Disney dog, but here 'Goofy' describes teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: Goofy teeth are buck teeth that stick out, so the adjective means sticking out.

clue.text: Sides in Brisbane and Tansmania for the final test

indicators.note: the sides of a word are its two outer letters, taken from each place name

explanation.surface: Teams in Brisbane and Tasmania contest the final Test match.
explanation.walkthrough: The Test is cricket's, but this is software: a beta test is the last trial before release.
explanation.definitionFit: Beta testing is the last round of trials of software by outside users before its release.

clue.text: Was Sir allowed to hold her back?

indicators.note: back means those held letters are read from right to left
to hold means the letters are contained in the run of words Was Sir allowed

explanation.surface: Was the knight permitted to embrace her?
explanation.definitionFit: Larissa is a woman's given name, so it stands for a female person.

clue.text: Triumphant cry from whaler cut short

indicators.note: cut short means the last letter of the captain's name is lopped off

parts.note: Captain Ahab is the whaler in Moby-Dick

explanation.surface: A whaler shouts in triumph, but his cry is cut off.
explanation.definitionFit: Aha is an exclamation of triumph or discovery, a shout of satisfaction.

clue.text: Can evidently make a winter journey far from trouble-free

parts.note: one who can make the trip evidently has the means, so the clue gives has
to sled is to travel by sledge over snow

explanation.surface: Someone can clearly make a winter trip that is far from easy.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as 'has sled': owning a sledge evidently means one can make a winter journey.
explanation.definitionFit: Hassled means harassed or bothered, so a hassled person is anything but untroubled.

clue.text: Rag some would say students organised the wrong way

indicators.note: the wrong way means the union's letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: the NUS, the National Union of Students, is the UK's organised student body

explanation.surface: Student rag week, some say, was organised back to front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rag' suggests a student rag week, but it is a tabloid; 'some would say' admits the jibe.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper, and rag is a disparaging word for a low-grade paper.

clue.text: Iced buns (four in total) at home consumed by daughter

indicators.note: four buns in total means two pairs, so the bottom word appears twice

parts.note: buns is slang for buttocks, a pair of which make an ass, so four buns make two
in means at home
ate means consumed

explanation.surface: Four iced buns in total, eaten at home by a daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Iced' is the slang verb for killed, not frosted.
explanation.definitionFit: To ice someone is American slang for to kill them, so iced means murdered.
